clue.text: Objects to putting work before raises

parts.note: OP is the usual abbreviation for opus, a musical work
to raise a question is to pose it, so raises gives poses

explanation.surface: Someone protests at work being put ahead of pay rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises' looks like pay rises, a noun; here it is the verb, as in raising a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to stand against it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Ham cut open with a can-opener?

indicators.note: the word for open is cut into, so other letters are put inside it

parts.note: overt means open, done in plain view
taken as written

indicators.note: the opener of the word can is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tinned ham being opened with a can-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the meat in the tin; it is the verb for over-the-top acting. 'cut' puts A and C (the first letter of 'can') inside OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor performs with exaggerated gestures, so to ham is to perform too theatrically.

indicators.note: finishing places the word for hit at the end, after the other pieces

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to ram is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A hit show's run is ending for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends was a long-running American sitcom; the question mark flags it as an example. The American spelling is the usual one for a computer program and is also used for a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends is an example of a television show, a broadcast programme.

indicators.note: the word for field holds another letter inside it

parts.note: to field a ball in cricket is to stop it

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of the word rice

explanation.surface: A paddy field in Asia with rice growing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy field' reads as one phrase, but 'Paddy' alone is the definition: a paddy is a fit of temper in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddy and strop are both British slang for a sulky fit of bad temper.

parts.note: the dead end up here: a place where a corpse is laid to rest, read as a pun on a road with no way out

explanation.surface: A road sign warning of a cul-de-sac ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is where the dead are finally put, so it is a literal end for them.

clue.text: Reeled off blushing — having received call to appear in court

indicators.note: the word for blushing takes in another word, which sits inside it

parts.note: a blushing face is red
to cite someone is to summon them to court

explanation.surface: A witness blushes on being summoned to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to say it from memory, just as a recital repeats words aloud.

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a business letter
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Following on from 4 down, a complaint about getting there.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie the surface to the clue above; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle of letters and images is a kind of brain-teaser to solve.

clue.text: Questions of ethics came out losing one point

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the fodder are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: E is east, one of the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: Ethical questions emerged with one point lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' tells you to drop E (one compass point) from the letters of ETHICS CAME before 'out' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious teaching text is set out as a series of questions with set answers.

indicators.note: not tells you to take away the letters of the following word

parts.note: temperamental describes someone moody and easily upset
mental means of the mind, intellectual

explanation.surface: A painting described as moody but not clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes MENTAL from TEMPERAMENTAL, leaving TEMPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk.

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
taken as written
the TES, the Times Educational Supplement, is a paper fit for an academic

explanation.surface: A professor is handed a well-chosen extra.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES is a British weekly paper for teachers; 'suitable' hints that this supplement suits a don.
explanation.definitionFit: To give money or goods to a cause is to make a donation, a synonym.

clue.text: Where pride comes before a fall?

definitions.text: Where pride comes before a fall?

indicators.note: comes before sets the word for pride ahead of the next word

parts.note: ego is self-regard, pride
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: The old proverb that pride goes before a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'pride goes before a fall'; the whole clue both builds the answer and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain indulgence that boosts self-importance is exactly where arrogance leads to a comedown.

clue.text: Hit singles? He'll want to do better than that

definitions.text: Hit singles? He'll want to do better than that

parts.words: Hit singles? He'll want to do better than that
parts.note: singles are runs scored one at a time in cricket, so a batter hoping for fours and sixes wants more

explanation.surface: A pop star wanting more than just hit records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit singles' suggests chart records; in cricket a single is one run, and the batter wants boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player at the crease hits the ball to score runs.

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A fortress of chic Parisian fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient citadel of Athens is a fortified stronghold on a hill.

clue.text: Split from Conservative to the other side

parts.note: the Conservatives are on the right in politics, so the other side is the left

explanation.surface: A politician defects from the Conservatives to the opposite party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft means divided in two, the past form of cleave.

indicators.note: the word for a bit goes round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a bit
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A pet setter dog is tame but a bit plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is a dog breed in the surface, but crossword setters call themselves ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal that has been domesticated has been brought under human control.

indicators.note: to ship goods is to send them off, read here as sending these letters away to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A handsome man met on a cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship' is an unusual signal for rearranging; the question mark nods to the surface, since a heart-throb met at sea fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy, attractive man is someone others swoon over.

clue.text: Bars where there's panic with dash to be served

indicators.note: served up as in a dish being prepared, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Pubs where a rush of panic hits at serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs, matching 'served'; it means obstacles, things that hold one back.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars and drawbacks are obstacles that disadvantage someone.

parts.note: the idiom for keeping a secret, read literally as the act of recounting a story

explanation.surface: Someone coyly refusing to reveal what happened on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That would be telling' usually means 'I won't say', but read literally it describes the act of telling a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating is recounting a story, the same as telling it.

parts.note: a hood is a gangster, and one who is robbing people through an illegal scheme fits

explanation.surface: Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The outlaw Robin Hood is evoked, but 'hood' is slang for a gangster who is robbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running an extortion scheme is a criminal who swindles people.

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea, so an event on the main is a boat race

explanation.surface: The headline attraction at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief'; it is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat race meeting is an event held on water.

clue.text: Don't come it if you want to stay in one piece!

definitions.text: Don't come it if you want to stay in one piece!

parts.words: Don't come it if you want to stay in one piece
parts.note: to come a heavy fall is a British idiom, so avoiding one keeps you unhurt

explanation.surface: A warning to someone taking a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is British slang for having a bad fall or failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy fall is what the phrase 'come a cropper' describes, so avoiding it keeps one intact.

clue.text: He's the first man emergency demands in crisis

definitions.text: He's the first man emergency demands in crisis

indicators.note: first tells you to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A doctor is the first person you need in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor is the person called first when someone is hurt.

parts.note: de is French for of
the TGV is the French high-speed train

explanation.surface: A traveller trying to leave a French high-speed train.
explanation.walkthrough: TGV stands for train à grande vitesse, France's high-speed rail service.
explanation.definitionFit: To get out of a railway carriage is to alight from it.

parts.note: read as a line of the dead, the procession following a coffin

explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession is a slow line of mourners following the deceased.

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
room means space, place

explanation.surface: A fine restaurant in which to eat curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like the dish; to curry a horse is to brush it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to brush its coat with a comb.

clue.text: Butcher's succeeding holding in sound of disgust

parts.note: the apostrophe s supplies the letter S

indicators.note: the word for succeeding keeps another word held inside it

parts.note: later means following on, succeeding
ugh is the cry of disgust

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop that comes next door, with someone groaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes from the 's of 'Butcher's'; LATER is cut open by UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to kill brutally, a massacre.

clue.text: It's found on board ships on a recce

definitions.text: It's found on board ships on a recce

indicators.note: found on board means the letters are carried within the following words

explanation.surface: Equipment aboard ships out on a scouting mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo-sounding equipment is used by vessels to detect objects underwater.

parts.note: grim means bleak and dreary

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word mouse

explanation.surface: A writer of a gloomy tale about a mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brothers Grimm collected fairy tales; 'bleak mouse' plays on Dickens's Bleak House.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm were German writers who collected folk tales.

indicators.note: flogging beats the words about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flogging a fake to a buyer, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' in the surface means selling; it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating storm, a tropical cyclone.

indicators.note: after places the gallery at the end, following the others

parts.note: taken as written
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A forger sells a phony to a gallery, continuing from the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain. 'fake' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To fake something is to copy it, a synonym.

clue.text: To a rare concoction — it will give you gas!

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are blended

explanation.surface: A rare mixture that produces a fizzy gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that pumps air into soil or water forces in gas.

clue.text: He is asked to stand to find a seat

definitions.text: He is asked to stand to find a seat

parts.words: He is asked to stand to find a seat
parts.note: a paradox of standing up to sit, resolved by standing as a candidate for election

explanation.surface: A theatre usher asking someone to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' means run for office, and a seat is a place in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward for election seeks a seat in Parliament.
